prompt: write pseudocode for binary search and give me its big-O complexity
text:
## Binary Search Pseudocode

```
function binarySearch(array, target):
    low = 0
    high = length(array) - 1

    while low <= high:
        mid = floor((low + high) / 2)

        if array[mid] == target:
            return mid
        else if array[mid] < target:
            low = mid + 1
        else:
            high = mid - 1

    return -1  // not found
```

## Complexity

| Case | Time | Space |
|------|------|-------|
| Best | O(1) | O(1) |
| Average | O(log n) | O(1) |
| Worst | O(log n) | O(1) |

**Why O(log n)?** Each iteration halves the search space. Starting with *n* elements, you can only divide by 2 about log₂(n) times before reaching a single element — so the loop runs at most ⌈log₂(n)⌉ times.

> **Prerequisite:** The array must be **sorted**. Binary search gives incorrect results on unsorted input.
